commitResults.messageBody:
Assertions record assumptions that should always hold given correct
callers, and are meant to catch programming bugs, not user input
errors (which already throw BotzillaException) -- so this only touches
places where a violation would mean the code itself is wrong:

- Task: name is non-null/non-blank, since Parser always rejects empty
  descriptions before constructing a Task
- TaskList.get/remove: index is in range, since Parser.parseTaskNumber
  already bounds-checks it against the list's current size before
  Botzilla calls these
- TaskList.getTasksOnDate: date is non-null, since Parser.parseOnDate
  only returns a successfully parsed date
- DateTimeUtil.hasTimeComponent: enforces the precondition already
  stated in its Javadoc, that the text was already parseable
- DeadlineTask/EventTask constructors: exactly one of each raw/parsed
  date pair ends up set, which toString()/toFileString() rely on

Also enable assertions on the `run` Gradle task, since JavaExec tasks
default to assertions off (unlike Gradle's `test` task, which enables
them by default) -- without this, running the app would silently skip
every assert.

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace magic-number substring indices with named command constants
commitResults.messageBody:
Command argument extraction relied on hardcoded integer literals
(e.g. input.substring(5), substring(8), substring(6)) that only
worked because they happened to match the lengths of command
keywords hardcoded separately as string literals in
parseCommandType (e.g. "mark ", "deadline "). The two were never
linked, so if a keyword were ever renamed, the matching substring
index would silently become wrong without a compile error, and a
reader had no way to tell what a given number meant without
counting characters by hand.

Introduce named constants (CMD_MARK, CMD_UNMARK, CMD_DELETE,
CMD_ON, CMD_TODO, CMD_DEADLINE, CMD_EVENT, CMD_FIND) in Parser
that are the single source of truth for each keyword, used both
for command detection in parseCommandType and to derive
substring lengths in the parseXxx methods via CMD_X.length().
Botzilla's MARK/UNMARK/DELETE handling, which extracts its own
argument substrings before delegating to Parser.parseTaskNumber,
now goes through new Parser.markKeywordLength() /
unmarkKeywordLength() / deleteKeywordLength() accessors instead
of repeating the raw numbers a second time.

This follows the CS2103 code quality guideline to replace magic
numbers/literals with named constants, and removes a latent
maintenance hazard rather than just relocating it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract duplicated add-task and mark-task logic in executeCommand
commitResults.messageBody:
The TODO, DEADLINE, and EVENT branches of executeCommand each
repeated the identical four-line sequence of parsing a task,
adding it to the list, saving to disk, and formatting the "task
added" confirmation, differing only in which Parser.parseX method
was called. Likewise, MARK and UNMARK repeated the same
parse-index / fetch-task / save / format sequence, differing only
in the keyword length used to strip the prefix and in whether
mark() or unmark() was called.

Extract this into two private helpers, addTask(Task) and
markTask(String, int, boolean), and have each switch branch call
the appropriate helper with its distinguishing argument. This
follows the CS2103 code quality guideline to minimize code
duplication: the shared persist-and-format behavior now has one
place to change, and each switch branch is reduced to stating
what's different about that command rather than repeating what
all three/two have in common.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract FlexibleDateTime to remove duplicated parsed-or-raw date logic
commitResults.messageBody:
DeadlineTask held one instance of a repeating pattern (a parsed
LocalDateTime, a hasTime flag, and a raw fallback string, used
together in toFileString() and toString() to fall back to the
original text when parsing failed), and EventTask duplicated that
exact same three-field pattern twice over for its start and end
dates. The same "parsed value with fallback to raw text" logic was
effectively written out three separate times across the two
classes.

Extract this into a new package-private FlexibleDateTime class in
botzilla.task, which wraps DateTimeUtil.parse()/hasTimeComponent()
and exposes toDateTimeOrNull(), toFileString(), and
toDisplayString(). DeadlineTask now holds a single FlexibleDateTime
field instead of three raw fields, and EventTask holds two instead
of six; getBy()/getStart()/getEnd() and the toString()/toFileString()
overrides delegate to it, so their public behavior (and the existing
DeadlineTaskTest suite) is unchanged.

This follows the CS2103 code quality guideline to minimize code
duplication: the "parsed-or-raw" fallback behavior now has exactly
one implementation to read and change, instead of three copies that
could silently drift apart.

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace instanceof-based date lookup with polymorphic Task.getDate()
commitResults.messageBody:
TaskList.getTasksOnDate() used instanceof to check whether each task
was a DeadlineTask or EventTask, downcast it, and then read its date
via a type-specific getter. This is a classic type-checking smell:
the caller has to know about every concrete Task subclass and what
each one calls its date, and adding a new dated task type in future
would require editing this unrelated method to add another branch.

Add a Task.getDate() method returning Optional<LocalDate>, with a
default implementation returning empty (correct for ToDoTask, which
has no date). DeadlineTask and EventTask override it to return their
deadline/start date via their existing getBy()/getStart() methods,
mapped to a LocalDate, or empty if parsing had failed.
TaskList.getTasksOnDate() now just calls task.getDate() and compares
it to the target date, with no knowledge of which Task subclasses
exist or how each one derives its date.

This replaces instanceof/casting with polymorphic dispatch, letting
each Task subclass own the logic for "what date does this task have"
instead of an external caller branching on type.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use streams in TaskList for filtering operations
commitResults.messageBody:
TaskList#findTasks and #getTasksOnDate filtered tasks with manual
for-loops that built up a result list by hand. This loop-and-
accumulate pattern is exactly what the Streams API is meant to
express more directly, and this increment calls for adopting
streams where they improve readability.

Rewrite both methods as filter-and-collect stream pipelines.
getTasksOnDate's filter delegates to a new dateOf(Task) helper
that uses a pattern-matching switch to extract each task's date,
replacing the previous instanceof/cast chain so the stream's
filter predicate stays simple.

Other loops in the codebase (Storage's line-by-line parsing, Ui's
indexed list formatting) don't map cleanly onto streams and were
left as plain loops.
Add assertions to document internal invariants

commitResults.messageTitle: Restore assertions dropped by merge with master
commitResults.messageBody:
The merge of master into branch-A-Streams (commit 1c128af) silently
discarded three assertions that master had added to TaskList via the
A-Assertions PR: bounds checks in remove()/get(), and a non-null
check on getTasksOnDate()'s date parameter. The merge tool reset the
whole file to this branch's side instead of combining both branches'
changes, even for remove()/get() where there was no real conflict.

Re-add all three assertions, keeping this branch's stream-based
implementation of getTasksOnDate() and its dateOf() helper intact.

commitResults.messageTitle: Restore FlexibleDateTime and getDate() in DeadlineTask
commitResults.messageBody:
The A-CodeQuality merge into master (f453aa6) was meant to bring in
DeadlineTask's refactor to use FlexibleDateTime (removing its
duplicated parsed-or-raw date logic) along with a getDate() override,
matching what EventTask already had. Comparing that merge commit
against branch-A-CodeQuality's pre-merge tip shows DeadlineTask
instead reverted to the old by/byRaw/byHasTime implementation with no
getDate() override, apparently overwritten by the IDE's merge tool
before the commit was made.

This left Task.getDate() asymmetric: EventTask overrides it correctly,
but DeadlineTask silently inherited the base class's Optional.empty(),
which would misreport "no date" for any deadline if getDate() were
ever called on it polymorphically. It also left FlexibleDateTime used
by only one of the two classes it was extracted for.

Rewrite DeadlineTask to use FlexibleDateTime and override getDate(),
exactly mirroring EventTask's pattern.
